# Filmweb — Polish retrospective

- Original source: [Chodź, pomacam Cię moim cepikiem](https://www.filmweb.pl/reviews/recenzja-gry-Robin%2BHood%3A%2BLegenda%2BSherwood-23254)
- Author / publication: Mariusz Kruk; Filmweb.
- Language / date: Polish; no publication date is displayed on the page.
- Access: Full review retrieved directly
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09
- Archived copy: lookup failed (archive.org rate limit); not checked
- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (commercial review, not transcribed)

Kruk awards 7/10, praising the characters, Polish dubbing, readable interface, and audiovisual presentation. He considers the campaign varied for one playthrough but regrets the absence of cooperative play and finds its strategic depth limited relative to its adventure-like appeal.

The retrospective is markedly less enthusiastic about playing it in the present: pacing and age undermine the experience for him. His claim that it has become effectively unplayable is an evaluative judgment, not a verified compatibility finding; elsewhere he reports no major bugs or severe frame-rate drops during his own experience.

## Detailed notes

Page facts: title "Chodź, pomacam Cię moim cepikiem" (roughly "Come here, let me touch you with my little flail", a line from the Polish dub); labelled "Recenzja gry PC" for "Robin Hood: Legenda Sherwood (2002)"; author Mariusz Kruk (user kruczek10); the page header also lists "Stéphane Becker" and "Jean-Marc Haessig" (game credits shown by Filmweb, not authors of the review); score "Moja ocena: 7" on a 1 to 10 scale; no publication date is displayed anywhere on the retrieved page; screenshots are captioned "Wanadoo Edition / Spellbound"; retrieved directly from filmweb.pl (copyright 1998-2026 Filmweb). Polish commercial review, not transcribed.

Review content, in order:

- Premise: the Robin Hood story would suit an action-adventure game (interesting characters, a good script, an archery system). A strategy game with the outlaw as lead was the last thing the writer expected of developers; hearing what Spellbound attempted, they were sceptical, but reviews and friends' opinions persuaded them to try. The game is dated to 2002.
- Fear of wasted potential: strategy games are not known for good stories, but here it is different. Besides "a great script full of colourful characters" there is "brilliant dubbing" in Polish. Many character lines have entered the canon; the internet is full of memes and clips of the "cult" dialogue.
- The player controls Robin Hood himself and assembles a team.
- Second fear: that the licence would be used to push junk. Not so: gameplay is interesting and very varied, "but only for one playthrough" of the single-player story campaign. The writer regrets that no cooperative mode was included.
- Interface praised as minimalist, intuitive and clear, which the writer particularly values in this genre.
- Number of locations is described as "quite a lot" for a game from the early 2000s.
- Main criticism: "little strategy in the strategy"; it felt more like a story-driven adventure game than a full-blooded real-time strategy. Skirmishes with various enemies were among the greatest pleasures. Occasional longueurs could make one doze off; the gameplay was not among the most dynamic.
- Audio-visual presentation "did a solid job in its day": practically everything looked and sounded nice, from character models (for an isometric view) to castle walls. Technically the writer finds nothing to fault except the long installation process, which they call a personal matter. They encountered no major bugs or sharp frame-rate drops, though for a strategy game it "demanded its share" of hardware.
- Verdict: for someone wanting to get to know the outlaw's adventures today, the writer must disappoint: the game is now fit only to be a museum exhibit; "playing this classic is impossible, because the tooth of time has done its work", unless one has played nothing from the last fifteen years. A pity, because it is "the last production" with this hero in the lead and the material is good. Robin Hood: Defender of the Crown (2003) also exists, but "is better passed over in silence".
- Score: 7/10.

Related titles listed by Filmweb beneath the review: Robin Hood: Defender of the Crown (2003), Super Robin Hood (1985), The Legend of Robin Hood: Conquests of the Longbow (1991).
